findings.desc: doc-code-drift: AGENTS.md:253,443,457,461,464,474,558 instruct running proof-or-stop testintent_record and proof-or-stop testintent_resume as live commands (concrete invocation example at line 464), but neither command exists in the CLI (node bin/proof-or-stop.js testintent_record --help / testintent_resume --help both return Unknown command; suggestions are testintent_handoff/test_add/test_list). Confirmed pre-existing on main under the old lattice testintent_record/lattice testintent_resume spelling, so the rename mechanically carried forward a pre-existing docs lie rather than introducing a new one -- but it remains a live, currently-instructed command in active docs that will fail if followed. testintent_handoff is a materially different command (generates a PLAN-phase handoff packet, not a human-override resume/record). High severity: command/flow error, not prose.

doc-code-drift: docs/requirements/decisions/role-prompt-modularization-and-budget-execution-plan.md:58,87,408 assert proof-or-stop-prompt-baseline.json currently records 16 roles ("当前 proof-or-stop-prompt-baseline.json 记录 16 个角色的最终 agent_prompt 输出"), and that dispatch does not send 16 roles at once, and a section header "16 个角色的具体修改方案". But docs/requirements/baselines/proof-or-stop-prompt-baseline.json actually has expectedRoleCount=17 and registry.agentCount=17 today, matching scripts/verify-proof-or-stop-prompt-baseline.mjs EXPECTED_ROLE_COUNT=17 and the 17 files under packages/main/templates/agents/. This file was edited by this exact story commit (d987989054 B-cdf6 CHK-003) yet the stale 16-count assertions about the CURRENT baseline were not corrected, even though CHK-003 explicitly targeted correcting the stale 16-count claim (per brand-rename-mapping.md:184, which says CLAUDE.md was fixed to 13-of-17). CLAUDE.md itself is now correct (17 total / 13 lattice-prefixed) -- this sibling decision doc was left contradicting it. Medium severity: prose/count drift, not a broken command, but it directly misleads a reader about the present state of a file this same story edited.

doc-code-drift: CLAUDE.md:836 gate table row for lattice-residue says the gate has two independent checks, covering [koala] and [brand-prose], and enumerates DOC_SCAN_ROOTS (README.md, CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, docs, packages/main/templates, .claude/agents, .lattice-codex/agents). But scripts/verify-lattice-residue.mjs implements a THIRD gated check, [brand-exec] (lines 380-399, CHECK 3), scanning EXECUTABLE_SCAN_ROOTS = bin, .codex, package.json, lattice.config.json, CITATION.cff, packages/utils/src for un-renamed lattice-cmd invocations, and it fails closed exactly like the other two checks. CLAUDE.md never mentions this check or its scan roots, so a reader relying on the table would believe the gate covers only two checks and would not know bin, .codex, package.json, lattice.config.json, CITATION.cff, and packages/utils/src are also gated for brand-invocation residue. This is the gate-scan-root widening the user flagged as done this story (B-cdf6 CHK-006 Pass A and Pass B per the script's own comments) that was not projected into CLAUDE.md's table. Medium severity: the code is correct and stricter than documented, no correctness risk, but the doc undercounts and under-describes its own gate.

doc-code-drift: docs/requirements/decisions/brand-rename-mapping.md's own Governing rule section (lines 36-48, 'Where the original table was wrong') explicitly disavows freezing tokens purely because renaming them requires coordinated edits, and names LATTICE_* env vars, bin/lattice.js and bin/lattice-codex.js filenames, npm package names, and .lattice/ state-dir-class paths as examples of WRONGLY frozen coupling that must be RENAMED-with-read-both-compat under the corrected test. The bin/ row (line 117) was correctly updated to RENAMED (additive) plus a kept alias, matching the corrected rule. But the Mapping table below still marks several rows in the SAME wrongly-frozen class as plain FROZEN with unmodified coupling-style reasoning: .lattice/ state directory (line 124, reason is renaming would orphan existing state -- coupling, not evidence), .lattice-serve.json (line 125), .lattice-codex/ (line 126), packages/main npm package @lattice/core (line 130), root npm package lattice (line 131), lattice.config.json (line 132), LATTICE_* env prefix (line 133), managed-block markers (line 134), lattice.remote-push-approval.v1 schema literal (line 135). None of these tokens are among the 13 salt literals hashed into stored _hash fields (the table's own stated sole criterion for FROZEN at lines 22-34), so under the table's own corrected rule they should read RENAMED (additive) with a read-both compat path plus a kept-name safety note, the same treatment given to bin/, not plain FROZEN. This is a self-contradiction within the story's own governing decision doc: the prose narrative (Governing rule) and the verdict table (Mapping table) disagree about which rows the corrected test actually reclassifies. High severity because CHK-006 checklist context explicitly states these are exactly the surfaces requiring the corrected read-both-compat treatment, and a reader trusting the FROZEN verdict rows would conclude no rename/compat work is needed for these tokens, contradicting the story's own corrected instructions.

CHK-006 (the largest body of work in the story per its own context: 146 LATTICE_* env vars across 245 files, ~20104 lattice tokens under packages/, 1360 under scripts/, bin filenames, package name, code identifiers, plus a read-both compat requirement) has verificationIntent={happy:[],edge:[],adversarial:[]} and verificationEvidence=[] -- zero intent, zero evidence, confirmed by reading checklist.json directly. This is structural: checklist_update refuses verificationIntent once an item exists in DEV (PLAN-only field), and CHK-006 was added mid-DEV. Consequence: all 36 must-intents in the story belong to CHK-001..CHK-005; the single largest, highest-blast-radius deliverable (touching read-both compat semantics and the .githooks/pre-push arming string) carries none of the frameworks intent-to-evidence coverage discipline. Recommend either (a) an explicit, durable waiver-style acknowledgment of this framework gap for mid-DEV-added items, or (b) retroactively binding CHK-006s already-existing DEV evidence (residue-gate/audit-scan regressions, read-both compat tests) to explicit intentRefs so coverage accounting is not silently zero for the storys biggest checklist item.
